newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-BRITAIN'S HENMAN WINS FIRST PRO TITLE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-BRITAIN'S HENMAN WINS FIRST PRO TITLE.

text.p: Rising British tennis star Tim Henman won his first professional title on Saturday when he outclassed Spain's Carlos Moya 6-3 6-1 in the men's final at the Sydney International tennis tournament.
Henman, a 22-year-old who was last year's Wimbledon darling, lost his first career final to American Jim Courier in Qatar last week and started Saturday's match as favourite on his form.
But baseliner Moya, 20, made a strong start and managed to break Henman in the third game of the first set with powerful and precise groundstrokes.

Henman broke back decisively in the next game and dominated the match from then on, taking 11 of 13 games. Constantly varying his pace and length, he closed Moya down with well-placed net volleys, big-point smashes and passing shots.
He broke the Spaniard's service three times in the second set, including the seventh and final game.

The win will propel Henman to around number 15 in the rankings, meaning that his three ambitions for 1997 -- to make the top 20, to win a tournament and to become a regular finalist -- have already been met.
He is also the first British male to win at the Sydney tournament since Vaughan Wilberforce Eaves in 1902 -- and he was Australian-born.

But Henman, who last year became the first British man to reach the Wimbledon quarter-finals in more than 20 years, said he was not too concerned about historical comparisons and preferred to focus on next week's Australian Open grand slam in Melbourne, where he has a first-round date with Australian "Scud" Mark Philippoussis.

"I'm not going to go in there and rest on my laurels for two weeks but I also appreciate that Philippoussis is a good player," said Henman, who picked up a winner's cheque of US$43,500. "Still, I think I can do well."
